newsitem.title: USA: Plans to hush Grand Canyon air tours delayed.
newsitem.headline: Plans to hush Grand Canyon air tours delayed.

text.p: The Clinton administration is delaying implementing tourist flight restrictions over the Grand Canyon National Park while it works out ways to reduce noise further, an Interior Department official said on Friday.
"The routes that took into account the free-fly zones did not get as much natural quiet as we wanted. We wanted to refine the routes," the official said.
The route restrictions were to have taken effect on May 1, considered the launch of the tourist season, but will likely be put off until next winter, the official said.
He said the administration felt it would have had to finalise the routes this week to give the Federal Aviation Administration, tour operators and pilots enough time to plan and train for them.

Other parts of the plan President Bill Clinton ordered to hush the din from air tours over the Grand Canyon, including phasing in quieter aircraft and dusk-to-dawn curfews, will proceed as scheduled, the official said.
